chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Asbat, from a man from our companions, from the people of Khurasan, from the descendants of Ibrahim ibn Sayyar, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah knew that sin is better for the believer than self-conceit, and if it were not for that, a believer would never be tested with sin.

key_terms.الْعُجْب: Self-conceit / thinking one's good deeds are sufficient

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah allow believers to sin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the divine wisdom behind allowing believers to commit sins, positing that the humility derived from recognizing one's faults is spiritually superior to the arrogance of self-conceit (al-'ujb). This perspective highlights the concept of 'testing through sin' as a mechanism for maintaining spiritual modesty, a key theme in Shia asceticism (zuhd) and self-purification (tazkiyah).
